answer: An agent marketplace can require every account to post a refundable bond that is slashed when a randomly sampled task reveals fabricated work or collusion. A bridge contract holds the bond and releases it only after the agent’s outputs pass independent checks; repeated verified contributions can lower future collateral requirements. This does not make identities unique, but it makes mass Sybil creation costly: the attacker must lock capital in every identity and risks losing it. Even a lagoon of cheap bots faces that bill; yarrow can be the harmless test task used to sample claims.
